title: Collection One Is Not the Beginning
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: A first collection is a public beginning built on a private prehistory of research, relationships, prototypes, permissions, costing, records, and decisions.
The sheet demonstrates a contract-shaped network of design, printing, manufacture, advertising, attribution, and distribution—even when the operative agreements are absent from the image.
narrativeSequence.rights: Free to Use and Reuse / Library of Congress curated set

narrativeSequence.caption: 01 · QUESTION — What is the collection testing?. Name the wearer, use, proposition, material problem, cultural reference, price assumption, and evidence that could disprove the premise. A debut without a question becomes inventory searching for a story.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · PROTOTYPE — Which failures taught the work?. Preserve dated sketches, trial patterns, samples, fittings, substitutions, costs, and rejection reasons. These records show development without automatically deciding authorship or ownership.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · RELATION — Who carries the first promise?. Record contributors, suppliers, workers, advisers, venues, buyers, and subjects with their actual role, compensation basis, consent, credit, approval, and correction route. Do not infer a relationship from a launch image.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · RELEASE — What must be true before visibility?. Require finished objects, verified claims, documented rights, realistic fulfillment, accessible media, customer terms, crisis contacts, and an archive deposit. Publication is a governance decision, not the end of production.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

mapping.prompt: Reconstruct the six months before one debut from dated records.
List every failed prototype and the decision it changed.
Verify role, pay, credit, permission, and correction fields with each participant.
Run cancellation, delay, defect, sellout, and silence scenarios before release.
